title: He waited.
paragraphs: Because love is supposed to rush… right?

Mary and Martha sent word: “Lord, the one you love is sick.”
Not a stranger.
Not a distant follower.

Two more days.
No movement.
No miracle.
No answer.
And if we’re honest, that’s where faith starts to crack.
Because some of us have prayed like that.

You called Him “Lord.”
You reminded Him of your relationship.
You believed He could fix it.
But He didn’t come when you needed Him most.
And now something in your life feels buried.
Gone longer than it should have been.
And you’re trying to worship a God who feels late.
But here’s the tension we don’t talk about—
Sometimes the delay of God exposes the condition of our faith.
Not to shame us… but to reveal us.
Because in John 11:6, it says that when Jesus heard Lazarus was sick, He stayed two more days.

Not because He didn’t care.
But because He did.
Some scholars interpret this as intentional delay for divine revelation—not neglect, but design.
Because if Jesus had arrived early… He would have been healer.
Because the real struggle isn’t just waiting.
It’s what waiting reveals in us.

The quiet disappointment.
The subtle accusation.
The questions we don’t say out loud:

“God, why didn’t You stop this?”
“Why didn’t You answer me?”
“Do You even see me?”
We start adjusting our theology to match our pain.

We lower our expectations.
We call it “maturity.”
But it’s actually wounded trust.
But deep inside… we’ve stopped expecting resurrection.
This is where it gets real.
Because some of us aren’t struggling with loud sin—

Delayed obedience.
Half-surrender.
Faith that sings on Sunday but doubts in private.
“I believe… but only if You move on my timeline.”
And that’s where Jesus confronts us—not with anger, but with truth.
When He finally arrives, Martha says, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died” (John 11:21).
But Jesus doesn’t defend His timing.
“I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live” (John 11:25).
Jesus is not trying to meet your expectations—He’s trying to transform your understanding.
Because if your faith only survives when God is early…
It will collapse when He is silent.
Are you trusting God… or just trusting His timing to match your plans?
Because the grave of Lazarus wasn’t just a place of death.
It was a stage for glory.
In Jewish culture, many believed the spirit lingered for three days. After that—final.
And that’s exactly when Jesus shows up.
So nobody could explain it away.
So no one could say, “He almost made it.”
So the miracle would scream one truth:
That’s why your situation feels impossible.
Because God is removing every alternative explanation.
Because what He’s about to do in your life won’t be credited to luck… or timing… or people.
But here’s the part that breaks me—
John 11:35. The shortest verse. The deepest heart.
He knew He would raise Lazarus.
Because delay does not cancel compassion.
Because even when God is working behind the scenes…
He is not distant from your pain.
Jesus didn’t come just to comfort the mourners.
He came to confront the grave.
Because Lazarus is not just a story about a dead man.
Ephesians 2:1 says we were “dead in our trespasses and sins.”
And no amount of effort, religion, or self-improvement could bring us back.
So Jesus did what we could never do.
Lived the life we failed to live.
Died the death we deserved on the cross.
Walked out of His own grave.
So when He stood in front of Lazarus’ tomb and shouted, “Lazarus, come out!” (John 11:43)—
Because one day, He would call all who believe in Him out of spiritual death into eternal life.
You don’t need a better situation.
You are not defined by what feels buried.
You are called by the One who brings dead things to life.
You are not abandoned in the delay.
You are being positioned for revelation.
Some of you aren’t waiting anymore.
And Jesus is standing there saying:
Trust His heart, not just His hand.
Let Him speak into the places you’ve already buried.
Because when Jesus calls your name…
If this hit you where you’ve been hiding…
Follow if you’re done with surface-level faith… God is not done speaking.
It might be the one that calls you out of what you thought was over.
